extracted.intended_audience: members of the Effective Altruism community and people considering grantmaking as a career or organizational activity
extracted.subtask_description: A short topic-page overview of grantmaking within the Effective Altruism community, describing what grantmaking is and how it's evaluated as a career option (including which attributes make it a promising path).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of grantmaking
rubrics_metrics.description: "Grantmaking is the process by which a government or an organization gives non-repayable funds or products for a particular purpose or project.",

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on top cause areas
rubrics_metrics.description: "Grantmaking focused on top cause areas is one of 80,000 hours 'priority paths'—the most promising career opportunities the organization is currently aware of.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicates a recommendation/criterion that grantmaking targeting high-priority cause areas is especially valuable; the page references 80,000 Hours' prioritization as justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career capital (as an evaluation criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Their medium-depth profile rates grantmaking an option with high career capital...",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to evaluate grantmaking as a career: how much relevant skills, networks, reputation, and future-options the role builds. The page cites 80,000 Hours' profile rating this attribute as high.

rubrics_metrics.name: Job satisfaction (as an evaluation criterion)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to evaluate grantmaking as a career: expected subjective satisfaction from the work. The page cites 80,000 Hours' profile rating this attribute as high.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct impact (as an evaluation criterion)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to evaluate grantmaking as a career: the extent to which the role leads to immediate, measurable benefits from funding decisions. The page cites 80,000 Hours' profile rating this attribute as high.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advocacy potential (as an evaluation criterion)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to evaluate grantmaking as a career: the potential to influence others, norms, or policy through funding choices and associated advocacy. The page cites 80,000 Hours' profile rating this attribute as high.
